lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write a survey question with four categories and show how you would tally twelve responses.

FEEDBACK
Any clear question + four categories + tally marks totalling 12.

WATCH FOR
Changing categories halfway through makes earlier tallies meaningless.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Design two surveys, collect or simulate twenty responses each and organise into tables with totals.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Question: Which fruit do classmates prefer? Categories: apple, banana, orange, other. Tallies become counts in a table.

TRY FIRST
Write a survey question with four categories and show how you would tally twelve responses.

FEEDBACK
Any clear question + four categories + tally marks totalling 12.
teach_steps.explain:
Collecting and organising data starts with a clear question, categories or measures and a tidy recording method (tally or table).

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Changing categories halfway through makes earlier tallies meaningless. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
